ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Toxicity as a reversible cause

An older adult taking digoxin develops nausea, visual disturbance and a new junctional arrhythmia after renal function deteriorates. Which evaluation is most directly relevant to a potentially reversible explanation for the rhythm change?

  1. Assess digoxin exposure, renal function and electrolytes
  2. Assume the rhythm is always a normal variant
  3. Increase digoxin before checking any laboratory result
  4. Diagnose isolated anxiety from nausea alone
  5. Exclude drug toxicity because the QRS is narrow
Answer and explanation

Assess digoxin exposure, renal function and electrolytes

Reduced clearance can increase digoxin exposure; toxicity may cause diverse arrhythmias, so medication and electrolyte assessment is essential.

Option explanations

Assess digoxin exposure, renal function and electrolytes: Reduced clearance can increase digoxin exposure; toxicity may cause diverse arrhythmias, so medication and electrolyte assessment is essential.

Assume the rhythm is always a normal variant: The new symptoms and renal deterioration make a benign assumption unsafe.

Increase digoxin before checking any laboratory result: Increasing exposure can worsen suspected toxicity.

Diagnose isolated anxiety from nausea alone: The linked clinical and medication findings require medical evaluation.

Exclude drug toxicity because the QRS is narrow: Drug toxicity can occur with narrow-complex rhythms.
